page: Amazon Web Services i7i.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, storage-optimized server featuring 192 vCPUs and 96 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8559C processor operating at 3.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Local storage is a key feature, with 45000 GB of bundled NVMe SSD capacity. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance across multiple domains. Multi-core CPU execution, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the top 10% of tested systems, though single-core stress-ng performance remains in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth for both small and large blocks is highly efficient, ranking in the top 10%, while the Passmark memory score sits in the middle 50%. The server demonstrates top-tier capabilities in database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput.

The Intel Xeon processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for deep learning. In LLM inference benchmarks, the server achieves top-tier prompt processing and text generation speeds for medium 7B models, and strong performance for large 70B models. Tradeoffs include average single-core CPU performance and average text generation speeds for smaller models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of local NVMe storage combined with massive DDR5 memory capacity reduces the need for external storage attachments, optimizing resource spend for data-intensive operations. This hardware profile is suited for large-scale databases, high-throughput Redis deployments, data warehousing, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
